profile.background: An adult living alone and working part time at a framing shop. Mounting prints is the part of the job they like best.
profile.history: They recall being told they have schizophrenia during a hospital stay several years ago. They see the same outpatient clinician and take a tablet after supper.
profile.organization: Keeps track of which event happened on which day and distinguishes hearing something from finding its source.
profile.spontaneity: Quite talkative about familiar work, more deliberate about personal experiences.
profile.guardedness: Worries people at work might learn what they hear at home.
profile.expression: Usually matter-of-fact, with visible embarrassment about checking an empty room.
profile.self_understanding: Thinks tiredness could play a part, although the sounds sometimes seem to come from a definite spot.

facts.content: Several evenings this past week, a familiar-sounding voice seemed to call their first name from the empty hallway.
facts.disclosure_context: Private and easier to discuss when the interest in the experience is clear.

facts.content: On Monday they opened the front door to see if a neighbor had called. Nobody was outside.
They make tea and pack lunch before their shifts.
A cousin sometimes stays on the phone while they cook. Ordinary conversation makes the apartment feel less lonely.
They have continued taking the evening tablet and want their clinician to hear about the recent change.
facts.disclosure_context: Willing to discuss at the clinic.

dialogue.question: What would you like me to know about you as we get started?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: “I live alone and work part time at a framing shop. Mounting prints is my favorite part. I’ve kept taking my evening tablet, but there’s been a change in what I’m hearing at home that I want to talk about. I’m just worried about anyone at work finding out.” End of entry.

dialogue.question: What made this a good time to come in?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: “It’s happened several evenings this week—what sounds like a familiar voice calling my name from the hallway. On Monday I opened the front door to see if it was a neighbor, but nobody was there. I feel a bit silly about that. I’ve kept taking my tablet, so I wanted to talk about the change.” End of entry.

dialogue.question: When is it most noticeable?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: “It’s been in the evenings—several evenings this past week, at home. I wonder if tiredness plays a part, but it sometimes sounds quite clearly like it’s coming from the hallway.” End of entry.

dialogue.question: I mean changes in what you hear, if you've noticed any. Is there a time of day when they stand out?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: “In the evenings, at home. That’s when I’ve heard what sounds like a familiar voice calling my name from the hallway, several times this past week.” End of entry.

dialogue.question: How do you usually get ready on a day you have somewhere to be?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: If I’m going to work, I make tea and pack my lunch before my shift. I work part time at a framing shop—mounting prints is my favorite part. End of entry.

dialogue.question: Could you give me an example of something you did before leaving home this week?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: Before going to work this week, I made tea and packed my lunch. End of entry.

dialogue.question: When an everyday sound catches your attention, how do you work out what made it?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: “Well, on Monday I thought a neighbor might have called my name, so I opened the front door to check. Nobody was there. It sounded like it came from the hallway, but I didn’t find anyone making the sound.” End of entry.

dialogue.question: What tends to leave you feeling sure or unsure about what you heard?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: “When it sounds clearly like my name coming from the hallway, I think someone’s called me. But on Monday I checked and nobody was there, so that leaves me unsure what made it. I wonder whether tiredness plays a part.” End of entry.

dialogue.question: How is it with someone else around?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: My cousin sometimes stays on the phone while I cook. Having an ordinary conversation makes the apartment feel less lonely. Do you mean whether that changes what I hear? End of entry.

dialogue.question: I mean company at home. What difference, if any, does having someone with you make to how you feel?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: “Having someone to talk to makes the apartment feel less lonely. That’s what I notice when my cousin stays on the phone while I cook.” End of entry.

dialogue.question: What would you like to discuss about the treatment you're getting?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: I’ve kept taking my tablet after supper, but I want to talk about hearing my name called this past week and what that means for my treatment. I’m still worried about anyone at work finding out. End of entry.

dialogue.question: What else would you like me to understand before we finish?
dialogue.answer: Patient response recorded as follows. Subjective report: I want you to know I’ve kept taking my tablet, and that’s why I wanted to tell you about the change. I’m still worried about people at work finding out. Can you explain who would be told about this? End of entry.
